text:
The Wild are one of the best teams in the West, and the question hanging over them is whether Quinn Hughes stays. Hughes and Minnesota haven't agreed on an extension, the Star Tribune ran a column telling him to make up his mind, and the GM has said publicly the Wild want to keep him. Meanwhile he has 16 points in his last ten games.

Minnesota is 15-3-4 with 34 points, an 11-game point streak and eight straight wins on the road. The process is strong, 56% of all expected goals (the quality of chances) and 52% at five on five, though the record runs ahead of it: our points model has them about six points above what the play has earned, almost all of it from goaltending. Jesper Wallstedt is 5-0-0 over his last five starts with .942 and 7.0 goals saved above expected, and the team has allowed 16 fewer goals than its chances.

The top line is ridiculous. Kirill Kaprizov, Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy have outscored teams 17-1 in five-on-five minutes together, Kaprizov has the league lead with 17 goals and an 18-point run over ten games, and Boldy had another hat trick in Toronto. Brock Faber just came off injured reserve and slid right back in.

Our playoff odds sit at 99%. What we'd watch: the Hughes talks, and reported interest in Dylan Larkin, because this is a team that looks ready to add.
